report.name: block-splits-run
report.why: Text either side of a block child lands on separate lines, with the block between them.

report.name: block-first-then-text
report.why: A leading block generates no empty anonymous block above it.

report.name: text-then-block-last
report.why: A trailing block generates no empty anonymous block below it.

report.name: two-blocks-three-runs
report.why: Every in-flow block boundary starts a new anonymous block; three runs, three lines.

report.name: inline-siblings-survive-the-split
report.why: Inline elements adjacent to the split stay with their own side of it.

report.name: display-none-does-not-split
report.why: `display: none` generates no box at all, so the run either side stays one run.

report.name: absolute-child-does-not-split-a-block
report.why: Anonymous blocks form around IN-FLOW block-level boxes; an out-of-flow child is not one.

report.name: inline-padding-baseline
report.why: Control for the two differential cases below: no decorations at all.

report.name: inline-padding-inline-axis
report.why: Inline-axis padding on an inline box advances the line: the text after it moves right by exactly the padding.

report.name: inline-padding-left-only
report.why: Only the leading edge: everything from the element onwards moves right by exactly it.

report.name: inline-padding-right-only
report.why: Only the trailing edge: the element keeps its position and only what follows moves.

report.name: inline-padding-inline-axis-large
report.why: The same as the 10pt case at 40pt: an engine that gets a FRACTION of the padding shows it here as a proportionally larger error.

report.name: inline-border-inline-axis
report.why: Inline-axis borders advance the line the same way padding does.

report.name: inline-block-axis-padding-does-not-grow-the-line
report.why: Block-axis padding on a non-replaced inline overflows the line box instead of growing it: the CONTAINER height does not change.

report.name: nested-inlines
report.why: A nested inline reports its own box, contained by its parent inline, both on the same line.

report.name: inline-wrapping-across-lines
report.why: An inline that wraps reports the UNION of its fragments — taller than one line, and wider than either fragment.

report.name: inline-block-sized-stays-in-the-line
report.why: A sized inline-block is exactly its declared size and shares the line with the text either side.

report.name: inline-flex-sized-stays-in-the-line
report.why: Same as inline-block: the OUTER display is inline, so the line is unaffected by the inner formatting context.

report.name: inline-flex-lays-out-its-children-as-flex-items
report.why: Inner display is flex: two sized children sit side by side inside a box that is itself in the line.

report.name: inline-block-wraps-its-own-text
report.why: The inner display is flow-root: a width-constrained inline-block wraps internally rather than widening the outer line.

report.name: atomic-inline-between-two-runs-does-not-split-them
report.why: An atomic inline is inline-LEVEL, so unlike a block it never generates anonymous blocks around the text.

report.name: flex-row-items-sit-side-by-side
report.why: Inline children of a flex container are blockified into flex items, so in a row they sit beside each other rather than joining one line box.

report.name: flex-column-stacks-items
report.why: The same three children in a column stack instead.

report.name: flex-anonymous-item-baseline
report.why: Two adjacent bare strings are contiguous text, so they generate ONE anonymous flex item. The marker records where that leaves the next item.

report.name: flex-display-none-does-not-split-a-run
report.why: A `display: none` child generates no box, so the text either side is still contiguous and still one item — the marker does not move.

report.name: flex-block-child-splits-a-run
report.why: A real in-flow child between the strings makes them two anonymous items with an item between: the marker drops by a whole line.

report.name: flex-absolute-child-splits-a-run-sequence
report.why: Unlike a block container, a flex container ends a text-run sequence at an out-of-flow child: the strings become TWO anonymous items, so the marker drops by a line even though the absolute child occupies none.

report.name: flex-blockifies-an-inline-child
report.why: An `inline` child of a flex container is blockified into a flex item, so it no longer shares a line with the text beside it.

report.name: flex-blockifies-inline-flex-to-flex
report.why: `inline-flex` blockifies to `flex` as a flex item: outer display becomes block, inner stays flex.

report.name: flex-inside-block-between-two-runs
report.why: A flex container is block-level, so it splits the surrounding text like any block.

report.name: block-inside-block-with-text-either-side
report.why: The nested block is a block-level child like any other and splits the run.

report.name: inline-flex-inside-an-inline
report.why: An atomic inline nested inside an inline flow box stays in the same line as the text around it.

report.name: three-runs-around-two-atomic-inlines
report.why: Atomic inlines never split a run; all five probes share one line while it still fits.

report.name: block-splits-a-run-that-was-already-wrapping
report.why: The split applies to the run, not to the line: wrapped text before the block still ends above it.

report.name: inline-block-containing-a-block
report.why: inline-block establishes a block formatting context, so a block child inside it fills its content width.

report.name: rect-of-an-inline-with-no-decorations
report.why: A bare inline still has a box: non-zero size, inside its container.

report.name: rect-of-an-empty-inline
report.why: An inline with no text has a zero-width box, not a missing one — it still has a position on the line.

report.name: rect-of-a-padded-inline-is-the-border-box
report.why: getBoundingClientRect returns the BORDER box, so padding is included in both axes.

report.name: rect-of-a-block-is-the-content-width
report.why: The plainest possible check that container-relative coordinates are right.

report.name: rect-inside-a-padded-container
report.why: Probes are reported relative to the container BORDER box, so the container padding shows up as an offset.
